speaker: villager
text: Good morning, swami. The bell rang sweet today.

speaker: villager
text: Riders on the ridge again... I do not like it.

speaker: villager
text: The Kurinji buds are fat this year. Twelve years, soon.

speaker: villager
text: Ilan carved me a sparrow. It sits on my window now.

speaker: villager
text: Kaali has been hammering since before the bell.

speaker: villagerF
text: Vanakkam, Aruvan. Stay for tea?

speaker: villagerF
text: Mind the chickens. They think they own the square.

speaker: villagerF
text: My grandmother saw the last bloom. She said the whole mountain sang.

speaker: villagerF
text: The well water is cold and sweet today.

speaker: villagerF
text: Thamarai is looking for you. She has that look again.

speaker: kid
text: Swami! Watch me spin like you!

speaker: kid
text: Is it true you can catch a falling leaf with your eyes closed?

speaker: soldier
text: For the Iron King!

speaker: soldier
text: Take the monk!

speaker: soldier
text: He is only one man! Surround him!

speaker: soldier
text: Burn it! Burn all of it!

speaker: soldier
text: Hold the line!

speaker: narrator
text: Before the monk, there was a soldier.

speaker: narrator
text: They called him Veeran. The Ash-Hound of King Dunkan.

speaker: narrator
text: Twenty-four years before the bloom.

speaker: narrator
text: The village of Thennur.

speaker: dunkan
text: Every roof, Veeran. A village that feeds rebels is a village of rebels.

speaker: veeran
text: There are children in those houses, my king.

speaker: dunkan
text: Then they will learn early what defiance costs. That is a gift, Hound. I learned it late.

speaker: rudhra
text: Come on, brother. Fire doesn't ask questions. Neither should we.

speaker: narrator
text: ...a child is crying somewhere in the smoke.

speaker: malli
text: Are you... the soldier who lit the fire?

speaker: veeran
text: ...Yes.

speaker: veeran
text: Don't speak. I'll carry you out.

speaker: malli
text: You're crying. Soldiers don't cry. Amma said so.

speaker: malli
text: My legs don't hurt anymore. That's bad... isn't it?

speaker: malli
text: Amma says... on the mountain, there's a flower. The Kurinji. It blooms only once in twelve years.

speaker: malli
text: She says if you wait for it... you become a little gentler, every winter.

speaker: malli
text: Here. Will you wait for it? For me? I don't think I can wait anymore.

speaker: veeran
text: I will wait. I promise you, I will wait.

speaker: narrator
text: Malli of Thennur. Seven years old.

speaker: narrator
text: That night, the Ash-Hound of King Dunkan laid down his sword...

speaker: narrator
text: ...and walked up the mountain until the clouds were below him.

speaker: narrator
text: He climbed for nine days. He did not know what he was climbing toward.

speaker: guru
text: Drink. Slowly. The mountain is not going anywhere.

speaker: veeran
text: Do you know who I am?

speaker: guru
text: I am blind, child. I know only that you are thirsty.

speaker: veeran
text: I burned a village.

speaker: veeran
text: I am no one.

speaker: guru
text: Then rest here tonight. Tomorrow you can begin to be someone smaller.

speaker: narrator
text: The first winter, he could not sit still for the length of one breath.

speaker: guru
text: Breathe in. Hold nothing. Breathe out, and let the fire leave with it.

speaker: narrator
text: The second year, he swept the same hundred steps every morning.

speaker: guru
text: You sweep like a soldier, attacking the leaves. Sweep as if each one matters.

speaker: veeran
text: They are only leaves.

speaker: guru
text: So were the roofs of Thennur, to someone.

speaker: narrator
text: In the fifth year, the old man gave him a new name.

speaker: guru
text: A man cannot carry two names up a mountain. From today, you are Aruvan.

speaker: guru
text: In the old tongue, a river. It wears its stones smooth, and sets them down.

speaker: veeran
text: Aruvan...

speaker: narrator
text: Twelve years. Every dawn, he waited for the flower.

speaker: narrator
text: Kurinji Mountain. The temple above the clouds.

speaker: guru
text: You breathe like a man holding a door shut, Aruvan.

speaker: aruvan
text: Twelve winters, Guru. Every dawn I still smell the smoke.

speaker: guru
text: Then let the smoke be your teacher. It rises. It does not cling to the fire that made it.

speaker: guru
text: Come. The bell. The village will not start its day without it — and Ilan will blame me, again.

speaker: guru
text: Go down to Kurinji. Thamarai has been asking for you. Something about her herbs and your "lazy monk knees."

speaker: thamarai
text: There you are. Hold this basket. No — with both hands, you're not ringing a bell.

speaker: aruvan
text: Good morning to you too, Thamarai.

speaker: thamarai
text: Neem, tulsi, a little ashwagandha for old Murugan's cough. He'll say it's bitter. Everything good is bitter first.

speaker: thamarai
text: Aruvan... the shepherds saw riders on the eastern ridge. Banners. Black and red.

speaker: thamarai
text: You were somewhere, once, before the mountain. Do you ever miss who you were?

speaker: aruvan
text: Every day, I am grateful he is gone.

speaker: aruvan
text: Sometimes he still wakes up angry.

speaker: aruvan
text: Who I was doesn't make a good morning story.

speaker: thamarai
text: Then let him sleep. Some people should stay asleep.

speaker: thamarai
text: Hm. You always do that. Answer a question with a closed door.

speaker: ilan
text: Aruvan! Look — a kingfisher. I carved the beak three times.

speaker: aruvan
text: It looks ready to fly away.

speaker: ilan
text: Can monks fly? Guru says if you meditate long enough you get light as a feather.

speaker: aruvan
text: Guru also says the moon is a lamp he forgot to blow out.

speaker: ilan
text: Kaali wants you at the forge. She says it's "important" in her scary voice. Can I watch? Please?

speaker: kaali
text: Monk. Those riders the shepherds saw — they're Dunkan's. Iron-eaters. They burned three villages in the south valley this spring.

speaker: kaali
text: If they come here, I want the young ones to know how to hold a staff. You'll show them.

speaker: aruvan
text: The staff is for balance, Kaali. Not for blood.

speaker: kaali
text: Then teach them balance. Hard. Use my practice dummies — they've survived worse than a monk.

speaker: ilan
text: Whoa! You hit like a falling tree!

speaker: kaali
text: You move like someone who has done this before, monk.

speaker: aruvan
text: Everyone has done something before.

speaker: ilan
text: ...What was that?

speaker: kaali
text: War horn. From the gate.

speaker: rudhra
text: People of Kurinji! By decree of Dunkan, King of the Nine Valleys, this mountain belongs to the crown.

speaker: rudhra
text: There is iron beneath your flowers. In three days, the slopes will burn and the mines will open. Be grateful. You will have work.

speaker: thamarai
text: Those slopes bloomed before your king's grandfather learned to lie! You'll burn a thousand years for a cartload of nails?

speaker: rudhra
text: A healer with teeth. Hold her.

speaker: aruvan
text: She is not yours to hold.

speaker: rudhra
text: Out of the way, holy man, or I'll — ...

speaker: rudhra
text: ...Veeran? The Ash-Hound — in a beggar's orange rags?

speaker: ilan
text: His name is Aruvan!

speaker: rudhra
text: Do they know, monk? Did you tell them about Thennur? About the houses we lit, side by side?

speaker: aruvan
text: They know who I am now. That is enough.

speaker: aruvan
text: Leave, Rudhra. Before I remember who I was.

speaker: rudhra
text: Who you are now. Ha. Water poured into a bloodstained cup is still red, brother.

speaker: rudhra
text: There he is. There's the Hound. I knew he was under there.

speaker: rudhra
text: Still the same silence. You used to go quiet like that right before the screaming started.

speaker: rudhra
text: The king would weep to see his finest blade dulled to a walking stick. Men — remind him what he is.

speaker: aruvan
text: I will not kill you. But I will not move.

speaker: rudhra
text: You still fight like him. You just stop at the end. That will get you killed, brother.

speaker: rudhra
text: Dawn after next, the king comes himself. Kurinji will burn, Hound — and this time you'll watch.

speaker: kaali
text: Thennur. The Ash-Hound. That was you.

speaker: thamarai
text: Twelve years you taught us patience. Twelve years! And you never thought to tell us you burned a village?

speaker: aruvan
text: I thought if I said it aloud, the mountain would stop forgiving me.

speaker: aruvan
text: What would it have changed?

speaker: thamarai
text: The mountain isn't the one you need forgiveness from, Aruvan. ...Go to the Guru. I can't look at you right now.

speaker: thamarai
text: Everything! It would have changed — no. Go to your Guru. I can't look at you right now.

speaker: ilan
text: I don't care what you were. You're still Aruvan.

speaker: guru
text: So. The past has come up the mountain on horseback.

speaker: aruvan
text: Tell me what to do, Guru. Fight, and become the Hound again — or stand still and watch them burn everything you taught me to love.

speaker: guru
text: Today, when you lifted the staff. Was it anger that lifted it?

speaker: aruvan
text: No. It was them. Ilan. Thamarai. All of them.

speaker: aruvan
text: Yes. And it felt like coming home.

speaker: guru
text: Honest. Good. Anger is a guest, Aruvan. Let it in, give it tea — but do not give it the keys.

speaker: guru
text: Then you already know the answer, and you climbed all this way to hear an old man say it.

speaker: guru
text: A blade is only a question. Who holds it is the answer.

speaker: guru
text: Twelve years ago you held it for a king. Hold it now for a flower that blooms once in twelve years — and you will not be the Hound. You will be a gardener with a sharp tool.

speaker: guru
text: ...The crickets have stopped singing.

speaker: aruvan
text: Fire arrows. Guru — inside!

speaker: rudhra
text: A message from the king, Hound.

speaker: aruvan
text: GURU!

speaker: rudhra
text: "Nothing you love stays." He wanted me to say it exactly like that.

speaker: guru
text: Don't... chase him with that face, child.

speaker: guru
text: The Kurinji does not hurry, Aruvan. And it does not hate the winter. It only waits... and then it blooms anyway.

speaker: guru
text: I never asked your name, that first day on the steps. I didn't need to. I could hear it in how you drank the water.

speaker: guru
text: Protect what blooms.

speaker: narrator
text: Guru Nilakantha, the blind abbot of Kurinji, who saw everything.

speaker: narrator
text: He ran until his lungs burned, and found only hoofprints. Then he came back, and sat with his teacher until dawn.

speaker: narrator
text: He stayed until the temple lamps burned out, and the stars went pale.

speaker: kaali
text: Here. I capped your staff in iron. Melted my father's old sword to do it.

speaker: kaali
text: Seemed right. A sword becoming something that doesn't want to kill.

speaker: thamarai
text: I was angry at you. I still am. But the Guru would have stood at this gate, so I'm standing here too.

speaker: thamarai
text: And these — the bitter ones. Chew them if you bleed. Don't make a face.

speaker: narrator
text: The village looks to Aruvan.

speaker: aruvan
text: We do not fight to win. We fight so the flowers outlive the fire.

speaker: aruvan
text: Today Dunkan learns what his Hound learned on the mountain.

speaker: aruvan
text: Make them bleed for every step.

speaker: villager
text: For the flowers!

speaker: villager
text: For Kurinji!

speaker: villager
text: For the Guru!

speaker: ilan
text: I can fight too! I've been practising on the dummies!

speaker: aruvan
text: Ilan. I need you somewhere more important. Run to the temple. If the gate falls — ring the bell, and keep ringing it until everyone is up the mountain.

speaker: ilan
text: ...Promise you'll come up the mountain too.

speaker: aruvan
text: I promise.

speaker: kaali
text: The ram! The gate's broken!

speaker: senthil
text: Please! Please — I'm from the river villages. They took me for grain, I never wanted —

speaker: aruvan
text: (Grain for sons. Like me.)

speaker: aruvan
text: Go home. Tell them Kurinji let you go.

speaker: aruvan
text: Your king made you a weapon. Weapons get broken.

speaker: senthil
text: ...My name is Senthil. I won't forget this. I swear on my mother's name.

speaker: kaali
text: ...He was just a boy, Aruvan.

speaker: thamarai
text: They'll come back with more. They always come back with more.

speaker: aruvan
text: No. This ends where it began. In Thennur — and then on his throne.

speaker: thamarai
text: Then come back. You promised Ilan. And I'll be very annoyed if you make me dig a grave in this rain.

speaker: narrator
text: One Kurinji bush. Blooming, out of season, where she lay.

speaker: aruvan
text: You waited here too, didn't you, little one.

speaker: malli
text: Are you still waiting?

speaker: aruvan
text: Almost, Malli. I am almost the man who could deserve that flower.

speaker: rudhra
text: Sentimental. I burned the east side that night, you know. You took the west. We split it like bread.

speaker: aruvan
text: We were boys who did what we were told.

speaker: rudhra
text: I still am. That's the only difference between us, brother. I never stopped.

speaker: rudhra
text: He wants your head on the fortress gate before the bloom. Let's give him a good story.

speaker: rudhra
text: There! Show me the Hound!

speaker: rudhra
text: Go on. Finish it. That's how this ends. That's how it always ends, for dogs like us.

speaker: aruvan
text: Go and plant something, Rudhra.

speaker: aruvan
text: For the Guru.

speaker: rudhra
text: ...Why?

speaker: aruvan
text: Because once, someone waited for me.

speaker: rudhra
text: He's on the throne, in the fortress. He will not kneel like I did, Veeran.

speaker: aruvan
text: Forgive me, Guru. I could not wait.

speaker: dunkan
text: My Hound comes home. Look at you. Thinner. Quieter. Did the mountain pull your teeth?

speaker: aruvan
text: It took my anger. I came to see if it left anything for you.

speaker: dunkan
text: You were my finest weapon, Veeran.

speaker: aruvan
text: I was your saddest.

speaker: aruvan
text: Leave the mountain, Dunkan. There is still time to be someone else.

speaker: aruvan
text: You made me a weapon. Now you will feel the edge.

speaker: dunkan
text: Someone else? I was someone else, once. My father left that boy in the snow. Warmth is something you take.

speaker: dunkan
text: Good. Finally, an honest word from that mouth.

speaker: dunkan
text: Sad weapons still cut. Come, then. Let us see which of us the mountain loves.

speaker: dunkan
text: I am the iron in the mountain! I am the winter your flowers fear!

speaker: dunkan
text: Then finish it. You know how. I taught you.

speaker: aruvan
text: You taught me how. A child in Thennur taught me why not. And a blind man taught me when.

speaker: aruvan
text: I don't do this for your throne. I do it so no child ever again has to wait for a soldier to become a person.

speaker: narrator
text: Dunkan, the Iron King, who was once a boy left in the snow.

speaker: aruvan
text: This throne was carved out of fear. From today, it is only a chair.

speaker: aruvan
text: Anyone may sit in it to be heard. Anyone. The crown stays on the floor, where it can't look down on anyone.

speaker: aruvan
text: Go home. Plant something. And if you have nothing to plant — come to Kurinji. We have more flowers than hands.

speaker: narrator
text: Year One. The mines were sealed. The iron stayed in the mountain, where it belonged.

speaker: narrator
text: Year Three. Thennur was rebuilt — by soldiers who once burned it. A boy named Senthil laid the first stone.

speaker: narrator
text: Year Three. Thennur was rebuilt — by soldiers who once burned it.

speaker: narrator
text: Year Five. Kaali hammered Dunkan's swords into ploughs. She complained the entire time.

speaker: narrator
text: Year Eight. Thamarai opened a house of healing inside the old fortress. Its doors had no locks.

speaker: narrator
text: Year Ten. Ilan, grown tall, taught the children to read — and to carve birds, and to set them free.

speaker: narrator
text: Rudhra came to the temple steps in the rain. He swept them for nine years, and never asked to be forgiven.

speaker: narrator
text: On the tenth, Aruvan forgave him anyway.

speaker: narrator
text: And King Aruvan, who never once wore the crown, climbed the mountain every dawn — to ring the bell.

speaker: thamarai
text: You shouldn't climb alone anymore. Your knees sound like Kaali's bellows.

speaker: aruvan
text: I have climbed alone every morning for twelve years. Today I would like company. But only at the end.

speaker: ilanAdult
text: The end of what?

speaker: aruvan
text: Of the climb, Ilan. Only the climb.

speaker: ilanAdult
text: The whole mountain is turning blue, Aruvan. Like the sky came down to listen.

speaker: aruvan
text: Twenty-four years ago, a little girl asked me to wait for this. I thought she meant the flower.

speaker: thamarai
text: What did she mean?

speaker: aruvan
text: Herself. She wanted someone gentle enough to be worth the waiting. I think... I am almost him.

speaker: ilanAdult
text: Don't talk like that. Please.

speaker: aruvan
text: Ilan. Ring the bell tomorrow. And the day after. A kingdom is only a habit of kindness, repeated until no one remembers it was ever a choice.

speaker: thamarai
text: And the throne? Who will sit on it?

speaker: aruvan
text: No one. Put it in the square and let the children climb it. It is the only thing a throne is good for.

speaker: rudhra
text: I swept your steps, brother. Every one.

speaker: aruvan
text: I know. They have never been so clean.

speaker: aruvan
text: Thamarai. Thank you for staying angry at me. It meant you hadn't given up.

speaker: aruvan
text: I was not always gentle. Forgive the old Hound for the days he got loose.

speaker: thamarai
text: ...Breathe, you stubborn old man. Just breathe. We're here.

speaker: aruvan
text: Yes. Let me breathe now. I have been holding this door shut a very long time.

speaker: aruvan
text: The smoke rises. It does not cling.

speaker: aruvan
text: Guru... I set the stones down.

speaker: aruvan
text: Malli...

speaker: aruvan
text: ...it bloomed.

speaker: narrator
text: Aruvan of Kurinji.

speaker: narrator
text: Once a soldier. Then a monk. Then a king.

speaker: narrator
text: At last — a gardener.

speaker: thamarai
text: The children ask for the story of the throne again. Tell it better this time.

speaker: thamarai
text: Sit for a while, Aruvan. Even kings are allowed to rest.

speaker: ilanAdult
text: I carved a whole flock this winter. The square is full of wooden birds.

speaker: ilanAdult
text: Guru would have liked this. Everybody sweeping their own steps.

speaker: kaali
text: No more swords. Only ploughs and bells. My father would laugh.

speaker: kaali
text: Bring me your staff. The iron cap needs a new edge, for walking.
